title.narrative: Emergency WASH Response for Drought-Affected Communities in Hudur District, Southwest state, Somalia.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtSomalia is facing a deepening and protracted humanitarian crisis driven by recurrent drought, erratic rainfall patterns, conflict, and large-scale displacement, all of which have severely compromised access to safe and reliable water for vulnerable populations. The 2025 Post-Gu IPC Analysis confirms that although the Gu rains started on time, they ended early in many areas, significantly reducing water availability in rural livelihoods, while forecasts of a below-average Deyr season further heighten the risk of prolonged water scarcity. These climatic shocks, compounded by insecurity and repeated displacement, have resulted in millions of people facing Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse, with rural communities and internally displaced persons (IDPs) disproportionately affected due to weak infrastructure, overstretched services, and limited coping capacity. Limited access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene is identified as a major underlying driver of acute malnutrition, high disease prevalence, and recurrent outbreaks of acute watery diarrhea and other waterborne diseases, particularly in rural and displacement-affected settings.ltbrgtIn Hudur IDP settlements and surrounding drought-affected rural communities, existing shallow wells are frequently non-functional, seasonally dry, or unsafe due to contamination, forcing households—especially women and children—to travel long distances, rely on unsafe water sources, or adopt harmful coping strategies. IDP populations, many of whom have experienced multiple displacements, face acute pressure on limited water and sanitation infrastructure, increasing public health risks, protection concerns, and tensions with host communities.ltbrgtIn response to these interconnected needs, MUDRO proposes a comprehensive WASH intervention targeting 775 rural drought-affected households and 1,900 IDP households, designed to address both immediate lifesaving requirements and longer-term water security in line with WASH Cluster standards. The intervention will include the development of new water sources, rehabilitation and upgrading of five shallow wells, and extension of water supply systems through pipeline connections from a newly constructed borehole to improve equitable access for IDPs and host communities. To address urgent gaps, limited emergency water trucking will be provided for the most vulnerable households for a three-month period. Complementary sanitation and hygiene activities will include the construction of gender-segregated communal latrines in IDP settlements and hygiene promotion focusing on safe water handling, handwashing, and disease prevention.ltbrgtBeneficiary selection will follow transparent, vulnerability-based criteria prioritizing the most at-risk households, while communities will be actively engaged from project design through implementation and monitoring. Community feedback and complaints mechanisms will be established to ensure accountability and responsiveness. Through this integrated and participatory approach, the project will reduce disease burden, mitigate acute malnutrition risks, and strengthen community resilience against recurrent climate and displacement shocks.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
